reason: Runnable and structural (HG norm test and root recovery over Z, no wall time), but as written it cannot discriminate. (1) Finite-size confound: at l=2..4 (dim 25/49/81) the achievable delta is far below the asymptotic JM limit (arm A itself only reaches HG 0.10 against 1/6), so 'never above 0.12' is guaranteed by small l. prediction_if_true is satisfied trivially and says nothing about the l->infinity ceiling. The 1/6 and 1/24 thresholds are asymptotic JM limits and are not comparable with finite-l success rates. (2) Resolution: the signal sought is ~0.01-0.02 in delta, while the grid step is 0.02 and the cells are binary success/fail over 8 trials. HG success is almost deterministic given sizes, so 8 trials add nothing and the grid is too coarse. (3) Bit size: at p=2^40, delta=0.03..0.10 gives |x|<=2^1.2..2^4 (S_4) and |x|<=2^3..2^11 at 2^56. The root bounds X,Y,Z are then 2-16, integer rounding of X and the LLL slack 2^((d-1)/4) (20 bits at d=81, 31 bits at d=125, against ~l*56 bits of modulus) are the same order as the effect. For S_4 the 'none at delta>=0.035' threshold sits below one bit of x at 40 bits, so it tests rounding, not geometry. (4) Missing null arms: no generic-polynomial control (random coefficients on the same Newton polytope with a planted root) to show whether S_3 structure matters; no unplanted-R control to measure the false-positive rate of 'heuristic success' (arm C's nontrivial-vector rule could manufacture successes); no above-reach negative control. (5) Arm A numbers (HG 0.10, heuristic 0.12-0.16) are quoted from memory and must be reproduced, not assumed. (6) Scaling to n=131 / 130-bit p: reach delta is scale-free in log p once p is large relative to dim, so the lattice result does transfer, but only via the asymptotic det accounting, which the toy as designed never computes. The toy also says nothing about S_5 (m=4, the lever that matters) except by trigger; S_3/S_4 reach is already known to be below the sqrt(p) need, so the toy can only confirm the closure or flag S_5. (7) Compute: not binding. Measured PARI qflll on random d=81 (56-bit, modulus p^4) 8 ms, d=125 37 ms. The 20-minute budget therefore allows far more than designed (bigger p, larger l, bisection). The cypari2/PARI/sympy toolchain is sufficient, no Sage needed.
fix: Redesign in three layers, all structural. LAYER 1 (the actual discriminator, no LLL needed): for each l up to 12-16 (S_3 dims up to ~900, S_4 up to l=4-5) compute exactly the log-volume of the helpful-only sublattice (log sqrt det of Gram of retained rows, in floating point via PARI matdet or numpy slogdet, or by the triangular/diagonal formula where it applies) versus the full JM box lattice. Find delta*_det(l) = sup delta with det^(1/r) < p^l/sqrt(r) (HG sufficient condition, 2^((r-1)/4) slack set to 0 for the asymptotic curve and reported separately). Report delta*_det(l) for arms A (full), B (helpful rows only), and B' (B plus the best row-selection by threshold on lambda.beta, scanning k), and fit delta*(l)=delta_inf-c/l; hypothesis is falsified only if B's fitted delta_inf exceeds 1/6 (S_3) or 1/24 (S_4) beyond the A fit by more than the fit error, or if B's delta*(l) curve crosses A's above the error bar. LAYER 2 (calibration with real LLL): at p ~ 2^256 (so rounding and LLL slack are <5% of the modulus), run qflll on arms A/B/C for l=2,3,4 (S_3) and l=1,2 (S_4), and measure per instance the continuous margin m = log_p( (p^l/sqrt(r)) / ||v_m|| ) for the first m non-trivial reduced vectors, plus the bisected maximal delta per instance (about 8 LLLs per instance), instead of a success-rate grid. 3-4 random planted R per (l, arm); variance across trials will be tiny, so report the spread rather than k/8. Report HG success and heuristic success (m vectors with a nonzero resultant over Z and the planted root recovered) as two separate numbers, as the idea already says. Check that the measured delta*_LLL(l) tracks delta*_det(l) minus the LLL slack, which licenses extrapolation to the asymptotic Layer 1 curve. LAYER 3 (null/negative controls): (a) generic-coefficient polynomial on the same support with a planted root, to separate S_3 structure from support shape; (b) unplanted R (no small decomposition) to give the false-positive rate of heuristic success and of arm C's nontrivial rule; (c) delta = 0.45 with S_3, where nothing should succeed; (d) arm A must reproduce the programme's measured HG 0.10 / heuristic 0.12-0.16 at the same l or the pipeline is rejected. Decision rule in the fixed unit delta (a pure ratio, no ops/time): class 1 closed if B and C stay within 0.02 of A in Layer 1 and Layer 2 and both asymptotic fits are <= 1/6 and <= 1/24; trigger S_5 only if the Layer 1 fit for B exceeds A by more than the error AND Layer 2 confirms the gain is not an artefact of unplanted-R false positives. Replace the S_4 delta grid 0.03..0.10 at 40 bits by delta 0.02..0.06 at p ~ 2^200. Expected CPU: Layer 1 under 2 min, Layer 2 under 10 min, Layer 3 under 3 min. Keep the non-genericity line: even an S_5 delta of 1/5 at finite p must be checked against B.D^2 << p before any claim, and everything is toy-only (no n=131 claim).
collisions: Helpful-vector pruning is the Boneh-Durfee / Herrmann-May technique itself, so the arm B gain is expected to be the known engineering 0.01 and the hypothesis 'class 1 stays closed' is the prior-favoured outcome
